value.option_title: Force-field error floor for coolant MD: an enlarged C10–C50 benchmark scored against measurement
value.question: Does GPU Green–Kubo MD of C10–C50 hydrocarbons and esters rank immersion-coolant viscosity and thermal conductivity the way measurements rank them?
value.hypothesis: Green–Kubo MD with one fixed force field has a chemistry-dependent error floor near 25 percent that more molecules cannot remove [s_ogbomo_res].

compute_axis.quantity: benchmark molecules scored against measured viscosity and thermal conductivity

held_fixed: LOPLS-AA force field with the closest prior's public LAMMPS settings [s_zenodo]
Green–Kubo estimators: three off-diagonal stress components plus heat-flux autocorrelation in the same trajectories
trajectory budget per molecule: 2 ns equilibration plus six 5 ns production replicas

predictions.if_lever: At 120 molecules, held-out viscosity error after bias correction falls below 15 percent and rank correlation with measurement exceeds 0.9 [s_ogbomo_res].
predictions.if_not: Held-out viscosity error stays above 25 percent and rank correlation below 0.7 at every set size, capping candidate ranking [s_ogbomo_res].
predictions.decision_rule: At 120 molecules, if_lever when held-out viscosity MAPE is at most 0.15 and Spearman rank correlation is at least 0.90 for both viscosity and thermal conductivity; if_not when MAPE is at least 0.25 or rank correlation at most 0.70 at every set size; otherwise unsure.
predictions.noise_rule: Bootstrap the molecules with 1000 resamples for 95 percent intervals on MAPE and rank correlation; a difference is real only if its interval excludes the decision threshold, and each molecule's replica standard error must be below 0.20.
predictions.expected_why: Published LOPLS-AA Green–Kubo runs already show chemistry-dependent errors of tens of percent that more sampling cannot remove [s_ogbomo_res].

value.compute_tested_why: The test varies the number of benchmark molecules from 8 to 120, which is exactly the work more parallel GPUs buy; per-molecule trajectory length is held fixed.
value.scored_against: Measured dynamic viscosity and thermal conductivity at 40 degrees Celsius from the public 835-molecule C10–C50 reference set compiled from Landolt–Börnstein and NIST Chemistry WebBook [s_ogbomo_db]; commercial single-phase coolant data sheets give property bands only [s_ef_visc].

sources.quote: We compile a database of approximately 4,700 critically evaluated reference values for the density, viscosity, and thermal conductivity of 835 unique organic molecules in the C10–C50 range.
sources.supports: the measured reference set used for scoring, its size and chemical range

sources.quote: Equilibrium molecular dynamics (EMD) simulations of eight representative molecules reproduce density accurately but show systematic, chemistry-dependent force-field errors for the viscosity and thermal conductivity.
sources.supports: the closest prior work and the baseline arm of eight molecules

sources.quote: Density is reproduced to within 4% for seven of the eight molecules at 40 °C. Viscosity errors are small for the pure hydrocarbons with LOPLS, but this property is consistently under-predicted for the oxygen-containing molecules; the reference ranking of the fluids is nonetheless largely preserved. Thermal conductivity is over-predicted for every molecule, by amounts that correlate with the density of aliphatic C–H bonds, compressing the reference range and misordering the fluids.
sources.supports: anchor tolerances, the predicted error floor and the if_not expectation

sources.quote: Only molecules with a dynamic viscosity of approximately 1–50 mPa·s at 40 °C were included, because this is the range accessible to equilibrium molecular dynamics (EMD).

sources.quote: a SMILES-to-LAMMPS builder for the LOPLS-AA force field, the equilibration, production and continuation input decks, and the analysis script that computes density, viscosity and thermal conductivity from Green-Kubo time-decomposition runs.
sources.supports: the independent code the protocol is built from and checked against

sources.quote: we verify that the viscosity of molecular liquids is not influenced by finite size effects down to systems as small as 250 molecules.
sources.supports: the 250-molecule box size held fixed across all runs

sources.quote: we find that a set of optimal values that effectively trade off accuracy with computational cost are tD = 2ns, tW = 2ps and tS = 10 fs.
sources.supports: the choice of a few nanoseconds per replica and the plateau check

sources.quote: an average of 10 short replicate simulations converges to the same value as a single long simulation. Since these replicates can be performed in parallel, the real time is reduced, although the CPU time may be the same or more.
sources.supports: running replicas as independent parallel jobs and the replica-spread noise rule

sources.quote: Conversely, L-OPLS-AA accurately reproduces experimental viscosities (within 15%) under all of the conditions simulated.
sources.supports: choosing LOPLS-AA as the single protocol force field

sources.quote: It should be noted that the rotational relaxation time, required integration time and ultimately the simulation length, increases by more than an order of magnitude with a relatively modest increase in chain-length (C10 to C16)

items.note: Research question framing what the plan will measure (whether GK rankings match measurement rankings); it makes no factual claim requiring a source, so the empty source list is acceptable.

items.page_quote: Viscosity errors are small for the pure hydrocarbons with LOPLS, but this property is consistently under-predicted for the oxygen-containing molecules; the reference ranking of the fluids is nonetheless largely preserved. Thermal conductivity is over-predicted for every molecule, by amounts that correlate with the density of aliphatic C–H bonds, compressing the reference range and misordering the fluids.
items.note: The source supports the qualitative claim of chemistry-dependent force-field errors in viscosity and thermal conductivity. It does not state a ~25% error floor (it reports viscosity errors from small up to 137% at 40 °C, with only four of eight molecules within 25%) and says nothing about more molecules being unable to remove the error; those parts are unsupported.

items.page_quote: Density is reproduced to within 4% for seven of the eight molecules at 40 °C.
items.note: This is the plan's predicted success criterion for its own experiment (120 molecules, error <15%, rank correlation >0.9) and needs no source. The cited quote contains none of these thresholds; it only reports the published eight-molecule results.

items.page_quote: the reference ranking of the fluids is nonetheless largely preserved.
items.note: This is the plan's predicted negative branch (error >25%, rank correlation <0.7 at every set size) and needs no source. Note the cited source in fact says viscosity ranking was largely preserved among the eight molecules, so the quote does not support this expectation as prior evidence.

items.page_quote: We compile a database of approximately 4,700 critically evaluated reference values for the density, viscosity, and thermal conductivity of 835 unique organic molecules in the C10–C50 range.
items.note: The protocol (LAMMPS LOPLS-AA Green–Kubo at 40 °C, six 5 ns replicas, set sizes 8/24/48/120, scoring on viscosity and thermal conductivity) is the plan's own design and needs no source; the factual kernel, an 835-molecule C10–C50 reference set of density, viscosity and thermal conductivity, is stated on the page. The page does not itself state the set is public/released (the article does release it) and most reference labels are database correlations rather than direct measurements.

items.page_quote: Equilibrium molecular dynamics (EMD) simulations of eight representative molecules reproduce density accurately but show systematic, chemistry-dependent force-field errors for the viscosity and thermal conductivity.
items.note: Quote appears verbatim on the page; value 8 matches 'eight representative molecules'; the record shows publication year 2026 and a C10–C50 dataset. The abstract says EMD (the article applies the Green–Kubo formalism at both 40 °C and 100 °C), so the item's 40 °C is one of the two reported temperatures, and the comparison is against adopted reference values rather than raw measurements.

items.page_quote: We compile a database of approximately 4,700 critically evaluated reference values for the density, viscosity, and thermal conductivity of 835 unique organic molecules in the C10–C50 range.
items.note: The page supports only the scale claim ('hundreds of molecules', 835-molecule reference set). It does not state that whether the error is a correctable bias or a random floor, or rank agreement at that scale, is left open; the work reports that viscosity ranking is largely preserved among eight molecules, so the 'left open' framing is the plan's gap claim, not a finding on the page.

items.page_quote: Density is reproduced to within 4% for seven of the eight molecules at 40 °C. ... Thermal conductivity is over-predicted for every molecule, by amounts that correlate with the density of aliphatic C–H bonds, compressing the reference range and misordering the fluids.
items.note: Both expected results match the page, and the carried value ('density error 4% or less on 7 of 8 molecules at 40 °C') matches the page sentence exactly. Minor caveat: the published run used 10 replicas of 8 ns with a 1.0 fs timestep, whereas test_summary specifies six 5 ns replicas, so 'repeat the published run' is not literally the plan's protocol.

items.page_quote: Only molecules with a dynamic viscosity of approximately 1–50 mPa s at 40 °C were included, because this is the range accessible to equilibrium molecular dynamics (EMD) simulations.
items.note: The applicability claims ('only at 40 °C for pure liquids between 1 and 50 mPa·s, not blends or sold coolants') are factual claims about the evidence domain and the item cites no source, so they are UNSUPPORTED by the rule. (They do match the work's inclusion criteria on the page I fetched, but no source is cited here.) 'Cannot show ranking behaviour beyond 120 molecules' is plan scope and needs no source.

items.page_quote: Density is reproduced to within 4% for seven of the eight molecules at 40 °C. Viscosity errors are small for the pure hydrocarbons with LOPLS, but this property is consistently under-predicted for the oxygen-containing molecules; the reference ranking of the fluids is nonetheless largely preserved. Thermal conductivity is over-predicted for every molecule, by amounts that correlate with the density of aliphatic C–H bonds, compressing the reference range and misordering the fluids.
items.note: The cited Spiral bitstream is the same article PDF (d6dd00260a.pdf) but returns unparseable PDF bytes; the identical text was confirmed in the published version of the same article. The quote supports the anchor tolerances and the qualitative error pattern, but not 'the predicted error floor' (no error floor is quantified) and only loosely the if_not expectation (it says viscosity ranking was largely preserved, and reports no 25%/0.7 thresholds).

items.page_quote: We compile a database of approximately 4,700 critically evaluated reference values for the density, viscosity, and thermal conductivity of 835 unique organic molecules in the C10–C50 range.

items.page_quote: We compile a database of approximately 4,700 critically evaluated reference values for the density, viscosity, and thermal conductivity of 835 unique organic molecules in the C10–C50 range.
items.note: Research question with no source cited and no factual claim to verify; its terms (Green–Kubo MD on C10–C50 hydrocarbons and esters, viscosity and thermal conductivity) match the scope of the cited paper, which includes alkane, alkyl-aromatic, ester and ether families.

items.page_quote: The MD benchmark, using a Green–Kubo protocol with quantified trajectory-length convergence, shows that the accuracy of the LOPLS-AA force field is property- and chemistry dependent.
items.note: The page confirms Green–Kubo MD with one fixed force field (LOPLS-AA) and chemistry-dependent transport errors that persist at convergence (viscosity under-predicted 17–38% for esters and 26–57% for ethers; thermal conductivity over-predicted +7 to +96%). But no ~25% floor is stated anywhere, and the paper explicitly says that with only eight molecules these observations 'can only be used to identify plausible explanations, rather than establish firm conclusions' — so the 'near 25 percent' figure and 'more molecules cannot remove' are the plan's own extrapolation, not page content.

items.page_quote: Despite these limitations, the force field largely preserves the ordering of the reference viscosity values for the eight fluids at both temperatures, suggesting that MD simulations remain useful for relative screening, even where its absolute viscosity predictions require caution.
items.note: This is the plan's predicted success outcome (what it will measure), which needs no source; the <15% error and >0.9 rank-correlation thresholds appear on no page and none is claimed to. The cited paper's finding of a largely preserved viscosity ranking is the grounding and does not contradict the prediction.

items.page_quote: these systematic under-predictions are unlikely to arise from incomplete Green–Kubo convergence. Instead, they are consistent with a limitation of the force field for the oxygen-containing molecules in this dataset.
items.note: Predicted failure branch of the plan; the >25% error and <0.7 rank-correlation thresholds are the plan's own and need no source. The page grounds their plausibility (force-field-limited, convergence-independent errors; thermal-conductivity ranking misordered) without contradicting them.
